characteristics: modular mission equipment including reconnaissance, EW, engineering, and weapons from machine guns to ATGMs (Kornet demonstrated)
Strength: Heavier and more modular than smaller logistics-focused UGVs like Kurier or Omich-2; single chassis can be reconfigured as transport, engineering, or combat vehicle
Limitation: As with most Russian combat-capable UGVs, actual battlefield deployment record is thinner than its demonstrated capability set
Estimated quantity available: Fielded numbers not disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the higher end of Russia's push toward a single modular chassis serving multiple roles rather than building separate dedicated platforms - the same philosophy as the Impuls family
contrast_vs_traditional: A modular tracked UGV capable of combat roles extends the same logic Uran-9 and the Ukrainian combat robots share: traditional doctrine assumed a crewed vehicle for direct-fire engagement, and a front where drone strikes and mines account for most losses gives every incentive to field an unmanned substitute wherever the mission allows it.

sources.label: Militarnyi — Russian unmanned ground vehicles deployed against Ukraine
